pairs.subject: canvas-graph
pairs.evidence: lib/kg/layout.ts:160 forceLayout feeds caller order straight into the O(n^2) simulation and never sorts canonically. An in-memory probe moved 80 of 80 positions when only the input order of an 80-node graph was rotated (130 iterations), and 21 of 24 for a star at the default 260 iterations, which contradicts the header's claim that the same node selection always gives the same picture.

techniques.evidence: lib/kg/layout.ts:160 Start positions are hashed from ids and output is quantized to 2 decimals (line 161), so repeated runs agree. But the layout depends on input order because floating-point summation follows array order. The 'order-independent' test only covers a 12-node chain at 60 iterations, where rounding hides the drift.

lib/kg/glyph.ts:73 The glyph module, which owns shape geometry, draws squares, diamonds and triangles that extend beyond r but exports no bounds or boundary-anchor function. Edge anchoring therefore has to fall back to a circle of radius r.

pairs.subject: canvas-graph
pairs.evidence: features/graph/graphLoader.ts:408 The loader places bulk contract nodes on a ring around their supplier at a slot hashed from the node's own id, so a contract arriving or leaving moves no other node. The force-layout core is fed from store reads ordered by id and by src,rel,dst, so its input order is canonical.

techniques.evidence: features/graph/graphLoader.ts:408 Slots come from node identity, and the contracts shown are chosen sorted by id (line 385). The layout runs server-side, off the interaction path.
features/graph/forensicView.ts:29 Edge identity is the src|rel|dst triple, which is the store's own composite edge key (lib/db/store.ts KgEdgeKey), not a bare (src,dst) pair.

features/graph/graphLoader.ts:377 The budget is sized from the measured high-percentile corpus: it caps contracts per supplier and reports the omitted counts in the payload instead of shipping about 150k nodes to the canvas.
